z-m-34-11.prereq.0: H3 is production difficulty only, not curriculum grade. Assume middle-school math and first Common Math “equations of figures” unit learned.
z-m-34-11.title: If you flip the slope upside down, do you get the reflected line?
z-m-34-11.topic: Shape equations: reflection in the line y = x (comparing two methods)
z-m-34-11.goal: Compare two ways to reflect line y=x. Decide which one reliable, then find and explain when reciprocal-slope rule fail (horizontal line).
z-m-34-11.material: Let l′ be reflection of l: y=2x+1 across y=x. Gaon say point (x,y) on l move to (y,x), so just swap x and y; get y=(x−1)/2. Jian say slope become its reciprocal and y-intercept stay same; get y=x/2+1. Both results have same slope but different equations.
z-m-34-11.thinking.0: Choose how to decide when two methods give different answers.
z-m-34-11.thinking.1: Find where a rule apply and where it no apply.
z-m-34-11.thinking.2: Compare methods and explain which one better.
z-m-34-11.prereq.1: Reflect point (a,b) across line y=x and find its coordinates.
z-m-34-11.s.s1.prompt: Which method reliably tell us which of the two results correct?
z-m-34-11.s.s1.hint.0: Choose one point on l and write (x,y), then write (y,x).
z-m-34-11.s.s1.hint.1: Substitute the point into both equations and check whether each one hold.
z-m-34-11.s.s1.o.a: The simpler equation more likely correct, so trust Gaon.
z-m-34-11.s.s1.r.a: Equation simplicity no determine if it correct. Test by substituting numbers.
z-m-34-11.s.s1.o.b: Both results have slope 1/2, so both count as correct.
z-m-34-11.s.s1.r.b: Same slope no mean same line if intercepts differ. Check whether only one l′ determined.
z-m-34-11.s.s1.o.c: Take a point on l, swap its x and y, and substitute it into both equations.
z-m-34-11.s.s1.r.c: Reflected point must lie on l′. One point fit show which result correct.
z-m-34-11.s.s1.o.d: Substitute intersection of l and y=x into both proposed lines, and check whether it lies on them.
z-m-34-11.s.s1.r.d: Point on y=x no move when reflected. The intersection must therefore lie on l′ too. This method correct as well.
z-m-34-11.s.s1.explain: Point (0, 1) on l move to (1, 0). Gaon equation works there; Jian gives 1.5, so e fail. Intersection (−1,−1) stay in place, so e must also be on l′; again Gaon correct and Jian wrong. Points: (0,1), (1,0), (−1,−1).
z-m-34-11.s.s1.acc.0: Intersection of l and y=x no move after reflection, so it must stay on l′. Checking which equation contains the point also reliable.
z-m-34-11.s.s2.prompt: What line do you get by reflecting l: y=3 (horizontal) across y=x?
z-m-34-11.s.s2.hint.0: Choose 3 points on l, then write their images after changing (x,y) to (y,x).
z-m-34-11.s.s2.hint.1: Check which line the swapped points lie on.
z-m-34-11.s.s2.r.b: Check whether swapped images of points (0, 3) and (1, 3) on l lie on y=3.
z-m-34-11.s.s2.r.c: Check whether point (3, 0), swapped from (0, 3), lie on y=1/3.
z-m-34-11.s.s2.o.d: No reflected line exists, because slope 0 has no reciprocal.
z-m-34-11.s.s2.r.d: No reciprocal means that rule cannot be used; it no mean reflected line no exist. Swap points and check.
z-m-34-11.s.s2.explain: Point (t,3) on horizontal line moves to (3,t). All these points lie on x=3. Reciprocal-slope rule no work for horizontal line with slope 0, but swapping points still works.
z-m-34-11.s.s3.prompt: Compare the methods and say which more reliable and when reciprocal-slope rule cannot work.
z-m-34-11.s.s3.hint.0: Check whether both methods work on every line, including y=3 and y=−x+4.
z-m-34-11.s.s3.hint.1: For each method, write one sentence saying when it cannot be used.
z-m-34-11.s.s3.selfAssess.0: Is my judgment based on test results (substitution)?
z-m-34-11.s.s3.selfAssess.1: Did I give an example where reciprocal rule fail?
z-m-34-11.s.s3.model.0: Swapping x and y for a point works on every line, so e more reliable. Reciprocal-slope rule cannot find a reciprocal for horizontal slope 0, so it cannot work there; you also need calculate intercept separately.
z-m-34-11.s.s3.model.1: Choose a point on l and swap x,y before substituting; that shows which equation correct. Reciprocal-slope method no work on horizontal line like y=3.

z-m-34-12.prereq.2: Distance from point to line meaning
z-m-34-12.title: Is the minimum distance between a circle and another line always the distance minus the radius?
z-m-34-12.topic: Shape equations: minimum and maximum distance between a point on a circle and another line
z-m-34-12.goal: Check how rule “subtract radius from center-to-line distance” change with line and circle positions. Organize minimum and maximum rules with their conditions.
z-m-34-12.material: There is a circle C: (x − 1)² + (y − 1)² = 4 (center (1, 1), radius 2) and another line l_k: x + y = k. You want to find out how the distance from a point P to the line l_k changes as P moves on the circle. Haeun knows the rule "The minimum is (distance from the center to the line) − (radius)." The distance from the center (1, 1) to the line x + y = k is |2 − k| / √2.
z-m-34-12.thinking.0: Test the range where the rule works.
z-m-34-12.prereq.1: Read center and radius from circle equation.
z-m-34-12.prereq.3: The position of a circle and another line
z-m-34-12.s.s1.prompt: Change k and check each time; choose your judgment at every step.
z-m-34-12.s.s1.hint.0: For each k, compare center-to-line distance with radius 2.
z-m-34-12.s.s1.hint.1: Draw the circle point nearest the line and the point farthest from it.
z-m-34-12.s.s1.st.0.ask: As point P move around circle, wetin be its minimum distance to the line?
z-m-34-12.s.s1.st.0.after: Line x+y=8 dey outside circle, so nearest circle point distance na 3√2−2. Rule work well here.
z-m-34-12.s.s1.st.0.r.a: This value na distance to point farthest from line. Minimum use the nearer point.
z-m-34-12.s.s1.st.0.r.b: This na distance from center to line. Circle point fit come closer than center.
z-m-34-12.s.s1.st.0.r.c: Haeun rule work directly here. Line dey outside circle, so nearer point closer by radius.
z-m-34-12.s.s1.st.0.r.d: 2 na circle radius. You no fit use am directly as line distance.
z-m-34-12.s.s1.st.1.info: Now k=4. Center-to-line distance na 2/√2=√2 (about 1.41), less than radius 2. Direct use of rule gives √2−2≈−0.59.
z-m-34-12.s.s1.st.1.ask: As P move on circle, what be minimum distance?
z-m-34-12.s.s1.st.1.after: If center-line distance less than radius, line cross circle. Some circle points lie on the line, so minimum distance na 0. Add a condition to the old rule: use am only when line outside circle.
z-m-34-12.s.s1.st.1.r.a: Distance no fit negative. Negative answer show the rule no fit this case.
z-m-34-12.s.s1.st.1.o.b: 0: line meet circle, so some circle points lie on line.
z-m-34-12.s.s1.st.1.r.b: When line pass through circle, some circle points lie on the line, so distance there na 0.
z-m-34-12.s.s1.st.1.r.c: Check which distance the absolute value represents. See whether line and circle meet.
z-m-34-12.s.s1.st.1.r.d: This na center-to-line distance. Circle points fit be closer.
z-m-34-12.s.s1.st.2.info: Keep k=4 and now find maximum distance to line as P moves on circle.
z-m-34-12.s.s1.st.2.after: Maximum na center distance plus radius, same rule even if line crosses circle. Minimum rule change with position; maximum rule no change.
z-m-34-12.s.s1.st.2.r.a: Even when line cross circle, farthest circle point lies opposite side from center; distance na center-to-line plus radius.
z-m-34-12.s.s1.st.2.r.b: This na radius minus center distance. It no relate to farthest point distance.
z-m-34-12.s.s1.st.2.r.c: Radius no become the maximum. Calculate distance to point farthest from line.
z-m-34-12.s.s1.st.2.o.d: Line cross circle, so maximum distance cannot be found.
z-m-34-12.s.s1.st.2.r.d: Even if line cross circle, maximum distance from line to circle points still can be determined.
z-m-34-12.s.s1.reflect: Rule worked when k=8; how you had to change am at k=4? Which point differ for minimum and maximum rules?
z-m-34-12.s.s2.prompt: Rewrite Haeun's rule for the minimum distance between circle and line l_k, add needed condition.
z-m-34-12.s.s2.hint.0: Compare center distance and radius at k = 8, 4, and 2 + 2√2 (about 4.83), and write results.
z-m-34-12.s.s2.hint.1: Make table separating distance and radius sizes.
z-m-34-12.s.s2.selfAssess.0: I distinguish formula for distance bigger vs radius bigger??
z-m-34-12.s.s2.selfAssess.1: Clear which case include boundary (when distance equal radius) on?
z-m-34-12.s.s2.model.0: If line and circle no meet, it is (distance from the center to the line) − radius, if dem meet or touch, minimum na 0. If distance no pass radius, it is 0.
z-m-34-12.s.s2.model.1: Only if d>r, answer d−r, and if d ≤ r the minimum is 0.
